about: Coca-Cola HBC is the second largest bottler of Coca-Cola products by volume, producing and distributing Coca-Cola, Fanta, Sprite, Monster, Costa Coffee and Finlandia in 29 countries across Europe, Eastern Europe and Africa. Revenue near 10 billion euros. Headquartered in Zug, Switzerland, with operational roots in Greece; Coca-Cola Company and Kar-Tess Holding are major shareholders. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (CCH) and Athens. B2B bottler that operates well-known Coca-Cola brands.

Dollarama is Canada's largest dollar store chain, operating over 1,600 stores with fixed price points across all provinces, selling consumables, household goods and seasonal items to value-seeking shoppers, and owns a majority of Dollarcity in Latin America. Revenue near 7 billion Canadian dollars. Headquartered in Montreal (Mont-Royal); founded 1992. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (DOL). Well-known Canadian retail brand.

Kimberly-Clark is a US consumer products company making Huggies diapers, Kleenex tissues, Cottonelle, Scott, Kotex and Depend, plus Kimberly-Clark Professional products, sold in 175 countries. Revenue near 20 billion dollars. Headquartered in Irving, Texas; founded 1872. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (KMB). In November 2025 it agreed to acquire Kenvue (Tylenol, Neutrogena) in a deal valued at around 48.7 billion dollars. Strongly visible household brands with a history of sports tie-ins.

Medline Industries is the largest privately held US maker and distributor of medical supplies, with over 335,000 products for hospitals, nursing homes, surgery centres and physician offices, and an e-commerce business. Revenue near 25 billion dollars. Headquartered in Northfield, Illinois; founded 1966 by the Mills family. Acquired by Blackstone, Carlyle and Hellman & Friedman in 2021 and listed on Nasdaq (MDLN) in a December 2025 IPO. B2B brand, little consumer awareness.

Wayfair is a US online retailer of home furnishings, decor and housewares, with Wayfair, Joss & Main, AllModern, Birch Lane and Perigold, offering several million products and opening physical stores. Revenue near 12 billion dollars and about 20 million active customers. Headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts; founded 2002. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (W). Strong consumer e-commerce brand with heavy performance marketing and occasional sports sponsorships.

Dick's Sporting Goods is a Coraopolis, Pennsylvania (Pittsburgh area) US sporting goods retailer with about 850 Dick's stores, Golf Galaxy, Public Lands and House of Sport locations, selling equipment, apparel and footwear online and in store. It bought Foot Locker in 2025 for around $2.4bn. Annual revenue is over $13bn. Listed on the NYSE (DKS), and chaired by Edward Stack. Strong US consumer brand, with sponsorship and partnership activity across leagues, college and youth sports.

Haleon is a London-based consumer health company, spun out from GSK in 2022, selling over-the-counter and everyday health products such as Sensodyne, Advil, Panadol, Voltaren, Centrum, Nicorette, Otrivin and Parodontax. It sells through pharmacies and supermarkets in more than 100 markets, with revenue about GBP 11bn and around 25,000 staff. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (HLN) and NYSE, with Pfizer having sold its stake. Many household consumer brands, and Haleon uses sports sponsorship such as Sensodyne in football and cricket.

Seagate Technology is a data storage company, legally based in Ireland and operating from Fremont, California, making hard disk drives, SSDs and storage systems for data centers, cloud providers, PCs and consumers. Its Exos drives power cloud storage, and it also sells external drives under Seagate, FireCuda and LaCie, plus Lyve services. Revenue is about $8-9bn. Listed on the Nasdaq (STX). Known by consumers through retail storage products, and a past sponsor of motorsport, including a long relationship with Williams F1 Team.

Amer Sports is a sporting goods group, now headquartered in Helsinki and listed on the NYSE (AS), owning brands including Arc'teryx, Salomon, Wilson, Atomic, Peak Performance and Armada. Revenue is about $6bn. Owned mainly by Chinese investors led by Anta Sports and FountainVest, which bought it in 2019. It sells apparel, footwear and equipment to consumers through retail, wholesale and e-commerce worldwide. Strong consumer brands, particularly Arc'teryx and Salomon, and a regular sports sponsor.

Huhtamaki is a Finnish packaging manufacturer, headquartered in Espoo, producing food and drink packaging such as paper cups, moulded fibre egg cartons, flexible packaging, labels and foodservice items for consumer goods and restaurant customers in more than 35 countries. Revenue is around EUR 4.1bn with about 17,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (HUH1V). B2B supplier; its products are everywhere in daily life but the brand is largely unknown to consumers.

Lazada Group is a Singapore-based e-commerce platform operating marketplaces in Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. Founded in 2012, it sells products from brands and sellers to consumers and earns commissions, advertising and logistics fees through its Lazada Logistics arm. Majority-owned by Alibaba since 2016-2018. Serves hundreds of millions of consumers across Southeast Asia. Very high consumer brand awareness in the region and previously sponsored sports events such as football.

Newell Brands (formerly Newell Rubbermaid) is a consumer goods company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. Its portfolio includes Rubbermaid, Sharpie, Paper Mate, Graco, Coleman, Yankee Candle, Oster, Mr. Coffee, Crock-Pot, Calphalon and FoodSaver, sold mostly through mass retailers and online. Sales are about $7 billion. Listed on Nasdaq (NWL). Customers are consumers and retailers worldwide, strong household brands.

Hanesbrands is a Winston-Salem, North Carolina apparel company making basics under the Hanes, Bonds, Maidenform, Playtex and Bali brands (it sold its Champion activewear brand to Authentic Brands in 2024). It sells innerwear and basics through mass retailers, wholesale and online in the Americas, Australia and Europe, with revenue of roughly $3.5 billion. Listed on NYSE (HBI); Gildan agreed to acquire it in 2025. Household brand with large consumer recognition.

Picnic is an Amsterdam-based online-only supermarket founded in 2015 that delivers groceries to homes using electric vans, in the Netherlands, Germany and France. It sells at near-store prices with free delivery and takes orders only through its mobile app. Investors include Edeka, Temasek and EQT, with about 1.7 billion euros raised. Serves millions of households. Strong consumer brand in the Netherlands.

Rappi is an on-demand delivery super app founded in Bogota in 2015 and now also headquartered in Mexico City, operating in Latin America, including Colombia, Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Peru and Costa Rica. It delivers restaurant meals, groceries, pharmacy items and cash, with RappiPay credit cards and Rappi Prime subscriptions. Backed by SoftBank, Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia with about $2.5 billion raised. Very high consumer brand awareness across Latin America, with sponsorship of football and events.

Trade Republic is a Berlin-based neobroker and savings app founded in 2015, letting Europeans buy stocks, ETFs, crypto and derivatives, set up savings plans and hold a Trade Republic card, backed by a German banking licence. It serves millions of retail customers across Germany, France, Italy, Spain and other European countries. It was valued at around 5 billion euros in 2025 and earns order-flow payments, interest and card fees. Strong brand among young European consumers.

Essity is a Stockholm-based Swedish hygiene and health company, spun out of SCA in 2017, making Tork professional hygiene, TENA incontinence care, Libero, Libresse, Bodyform, Leukoplast and JOBST products. It sells in about 150 countries, with revenue near SEK 140 billion and about 36,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (ESSITY-B). Customers are consumers, healthcare and businesses. Many strong consumer brands in Europe, including Libero and Bodyform.

Sealed Air is a Charlotte, North Carolina packaging company known for Cryovac food packaging and Bubble Wrap, Sealed Air Protective and Autobag. It serves food processors, retailers, e-commerce and industrial customers in about 120 countries, with revenue near $5.4 billion and roughly 16,000 employees. Listed on NYSE (SEE). Customers are businesses, not consumers. Bubble Wrap is a household name, though the company is B2B.

Whatnot is a Los Angeles-based live shopping marketplace, founded in 2019, where sellers sell collectibles such as trading cards, sneakers, comics, toys and fashion by live video, and buyers bid in real time via the app. It operates in the US, UK and Germany, earning commissions. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz, CapitalG and DST, and valued at about $5 billion in 2025. Strong consumer brand among collectors and growing in live commerce.

American Greetings is a Westlake, Ohio greeting card and social expression company, founded in 1906, which sells cards, gift wrap, party goods and the Carlton Cards brand, as well as online e-cards (the American Greetings and Egreetings sites). It also owns the Strawberry Shortcake and Care Bears properties via the former AG Properties. It is privately held, owned by the Weiss family and investors. Customers are consumers and retailers. High consumer brand awareness in North America.

Upexi is a Tampa, Florida-based brand owner focused on direct-to-consumer and Amazon-channel products, including dietary supplements, pet and wellness products, and lately a Solana treasury strategy. Listed on Nasdaq (UPXI). Customers are online consumers. It reports funding of about $882 million, mostly from a 2025 Solana treasury raise. Small cap, low consumer brand awareness.

about: Zetwerk is a Bengaluru-based Indian business-to-business manufacturing marketplace and platform, founded in 2018, linking buyers with a network of suppliers to produce custom components, machinery and infrastructure goods, from castings to solar and electronics. Customers are corporates in sectors from aerospace to energy across India and the US. Backed by Sequoia, Kae and Greenoaks with about $964 million raised. B2B, with limited consumer awareness.

Reliance Retail is India's largest retailer, a subsidiary of Reliance Industries headquartered in Mumbai, operating over 18,000 stores across grocery (Reliance Smart, Fresh), fashion (Trends, Ajio), electronics (Reliance Digital), jewellery, pharmacy and online JioMart. Revenue is around 3 trillion rupees. Customers are mass-market Indian shoppers. Founded 2006. Very strong consumer brand across India, with sponsorship of cricket and other sports through the Reliance group.

Walmart is the world's largest retailer by revenue, headquartered in Bentonville, Arkansas and listed on the NYSE and Nasdaq (WMT), operating around 10,500 stores in 19 countries including Walmart US, Sam's Club, Walmart International and Flipkart/PhonePe stakes, with about 2.1 million employees and revenue above 640 billion dollars. Founded 1962 by Sam Walton. Customers are mainstream shoppers; also runs advertising (Walmart Connect). Extremely recognisable consumer brand with a large advertising business of its own.

ITC Limited is an Indian multi-business conglomerate headquartered in Kolkata and listed on the NSE and BSE, with businesses in cigarettes, FMCG foods (Aashirvaad, Sunfeast, Bingo, Yippee, B Natural), personal care, paper and packaging, agri-business and luxury hotels (ITC Hotels). British American Tobacco is a large shareholder. Revenue is about 750 billion rupees. Founded 1910 as Imperial Tobacco. Many strong mass-market consumer brands with heavy advertising.

Primo Brands is a North American bottled water and drinking water solutions company, headquartered in Tampa, Florida and listed on the NYSE (PRMB). It was created in November 2024 by the merger of Primo Water and BlueTriton, owning Poland Spring, Pure Life, Deer Park, Arrowhead, Ozarka, Saratoga, Mountain Valley, plus water dispensers, exchange and refill services. Revenue is about 7 billion dollars, with delivery to homes and offices. Strong consumer brands in US supermarkets and convenience stores.

Atlanta-based pest control company, founded 1948, operating Orkin, Terminix (after 2024), Western and Northwest Exterminating branches. Residential and commercial customers across North America, Australia and Europe, paying recurring service fees. Revenue about $3.5 billion. Listed on the NYSE (ROL). Orkin is a well-known consumer brand in the US. Rollins employs about 20,000 people, has more than 800 branches, and is known for its Orkin and Terminix brands.

Boston-based Amazon seller aggregator, founded 2018, which acquired hundreds of third-party Amazon brands and was restructured in a 2024 bankruptcy. Brands included small household and consumer products. Funding of about $3.4 billion shown. Low brand awareness among consumers. Customers bought through Amazon Marketplace, where the group sold under many third-party brand names. Little public brand recognition. Thrasio once raised billions from investors and acquired more than 200 brands before restructuring left it much smaller.

Beijing-based fresh grocery e-commerce platform, Missfresh, founded 2014, delivering groceries in under an hour. It ceased most operations around 2022-23. Funding shown is about $1.7 billion. Not a current sponsorship prospect. Pioneer of the grocery front-warehouse model in China. Previously backed by Tencent, Walmart and Alibaba. Missfresh's founders built a network of local mini-warehouses before the company ran into funding trouble and halted most services.

El Paso-based consumer products company owning Hydro Flask, OXO, Honeywell, Vicks, Braun and Drybar brands. Revenue about $2 billion. Listed on Nasdaq (HELE). Strong consumer brand portfolio sold through retailers. Revenue is about $2 billion with brands sold through retailers and online, in over 100 countries. Helen of Troy employs about 2,000 people and sells household appliances, health and beauty products and outdoor gear.

Jumia is the largest pan-African e-commerce platform, operating a marketplace, logistics network (Jumia Logistics) and payment service (JumiaPay) in markets including Nigeria, Egypt, Morocco, Kenya and Ivory Coast. It sells electronics, fashion and household goods from third-party sellers to consumers and earns commissions, fulfilment fees and advertising. Founded in 2012, headquartered in Lagos with corporate roots in Berlin, it listed on the NYSE (JMIA) in 2019. Well-known consumer brand across Africa with tens of millions of visitors, little recognition elsewhere.

Ozon is Russia's largest e-commerce platform, a multi-category marketplace selling electronics, fashion, groceries and household goods with its own logistics, a fintech arm (Ozon Bank) and a seller marketplace. Founded in 1998 and based in Moscow, it listed on Nasdaq in 2020, which was a first for a Russian internet company. Its Nasdaq trading was suspended after 2022 sanctions and Russia's invasion of Ukraine, and the group was reorganised under Russian ownership. Tens of millions of active buyers and very high brand awareness in Russia, but no international reach and sanctions exposure.

Groupe SEB is the French small domestic appliances and cookware group behind Tefal, Krups, Rowenta, Moulinex, Seb, WMF, Lagostina and Supor. It sells kitchen, home-care and personal care products through retailers and professional coffee machines to commercial customers in 150 countries, with sales above 8 billion euros and about 33,000 employees. Founded in 1857, headquartered in Ecully near Lyon (Crunchbase shows Carros), listed on Euronext Paris (SK), with the Peugeot-family holding company FFP and Venelle controlling shares. Household brands with broad consumer recognition worldwide.

InterVest Capital Partners is a New York-based asset-based lender, according to the Crunchbase description, providing consumer and commercial financing. Crunchbase industries list consumer and financial services. The funding amount shown is 867 million dollars. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Myntra is an Indian online fashion and lifestyle marketplace founded in 2007, headquartered in Bengaluru and owned by Flipkart, which acquired it in 2014 and also owns its sister brand Jabong. It sells clothing, footwear and accessories from thousands of brands, runs its own private labels like Roadster and HRX, and hosts the End of Reason Sale. Customers are consumers across India, with tens of millions of users. Strong consumer brand in India; Flipkart, in turn, is majority owned by Walmart.

WASH is a US laundry room management company, historically known as WASH Multifamily Laundry Systems, which supplies and services coin and app-operated washers and dryers in apartment buildings, student housing and hospitality. Customers are property owners and managers, and it shares laundry revenue with them. Headquartered in Torrance, California, it is owned by private equity and large investors (Crunchbase shows funding of about 850 million dollars). Large route-based operator in more than 40 states. Recognised by residents on site but little general consumer brand awareness.

B2B2C brand with little awareness outside HR and benefits teams.

about: Zum is a Redwood City, California, school transportation company that provides student buses and routing technology for school districts in the United States, including electric school buses, and also offers child care transport. Founded in 2014, it has contracts with large districts such as Oakland and Seattle, and has raised funding of about 500 million dollars. Customers are school districts and parents. Local brand recognition among families in its districts.

Prestige Consumer Healthcare is a US marketer of over-the-counter healthcare brands, such as Monistat, Dramamine, Summer's Eve, Clear Eyes, Chloraseptic and BC/Goody's powders, sold in drugstores and supermarkets. It does not manufacture, using contract manufacturers. Based in Tarrytown, New York, and listed on the NYSE (PBH), it has revenue of about 1.1 billion dollars. Customers are US consumers; products have strong shelf presence in pharmacies, but the corporate name is little known.

Tata group's digital commerce arm, based in Mumbai, behind the Tata Neu super app, BigBasket, 1mg, Croma and other consumer brands, covering grocery, pharmacy, electronics and payments in India. Subsidiary of Tata Sons. Consumer brand with large reach and strong awareness in India, supported by Tata group credibility.

US discount retailer based in Goodlettsville, Tennessee, with about 20,000 small-box stores selling basic groceries, household goods and apparel, mostly in rural and small-town communities. Listed on the NYSE (DG). Revenue about USD 40 billion. The company dates to 1939 and now operates in about 48 states, with the pOpshelf concept and DG Market small-format stores alongside its core Dollar General stores. It targets low and fixed-income shoppers within a short drive of home. Strong consumer brand across the US, with motorsport sponsorship.

Hangzhou-based Chinese home furnishings company, Kuka Home, making sofas, beds, mattresses and furniture sold through stores in China and exported to overseas markets. Listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. Consumer brand with strong awareness in China and moderate presence abroad.

about: Peruvian consumer goods and food group based in Lima, making cooking oils, pasta, flour, detergents, and personal care brands such as Primor, Don Vittorio and Bolivar. Listed on the Lima exchange (ALICORC1) and part of the Romero group. Sells in Peru, Bolivia, Ecuador and other Latin American markets. Mass-market consumer brands, with very strong awareness in Peru.

US fishing tackle company based in Columbia, South Carolina, whose brands include Berkley, Abu Garcia, Penn, Shakespeare and Sebile, sold through outdoor retailers worldwide. Customers are anglers. It is private and part of a larger consumer products owner. Moderately known to fishing and outdoor audiences, with tournament sponsorships.

about: US household products company based in Lake Forest, Illinois, making Reynolds Wrap aluminium foil, Hefty trash and storage bags and Presto food bags.
